title: Biggest Ships in the World
period_label: One card per ship class · In service Nov 2026
source_line: Sources: DNV Vessel Register, VesselFinder · Flag = operator HQ
scope_note: What counts: every ship class in service in Nov 2026 bigger than the largest oil tanker still trading (170,618 GT), ranked by registered gross tonnage (GT, enclosed volume, not weight). Sister ships share one card; the value is the largest ship of the class. Moored units (FPSO, FLNG, storage tankers) and warships are excluded. Flags show the operating company's HQ, not the flag of registry: OOCL is listed under Hong Kong, ONE (a Japanese joint venture) under Singapore, Valemax/Guaibamax under Brazil (built for and chartered to Vale).

layout.image_prefer: a real photo of this exact ship (or a named sister ship of the same class) at sea or in port, whole hull visible bow to stern, three-quarter bow view preferred

items.name: Pioneering Spirit
items.subtitle: Crane vessel · one of a kind

source.name: Lloyd's Register via Wikipedia & VesselFinder: Pioneering Spirit (IMO 9593505), GT 403,342; Allseas spec sheet

items.notes: Twin-hull platform installation/decommissioning vessel. Hull built by DSME (South Korea), 2014; completed in the Netherlands and in service since 2016. Allseas spec sheet: 382 m (477 m incl. stinger) x 124 m, topsides lift 48,000 t.
items.image_hint: photo of Pioneering Spirit (IMO 9593505) or a named sister of the Pioneering Spirit; Twin-hull (split-hull) crane vessel, 382 m x 124 m; a 122 m-long slot cut into the bow between the two hulls; eight huge yellow topsides-lift beams at the bow; white/grey superstructure and helideck at the stern; 'ALLSEAS' on the hull. Exclude: Not Allseas' pipelayers Solitaire/Audacia; not Heerema's semi-submersible crane vessels Sleipnir or Thialf (red cranes on columns); not the Prelude FLNG. View: Bow three-quarter view at sea or in the Maasvlakte/Rotterdam area, showing the bow slot and yellow lift beams.

insights.text: No oil tanker makes this list: the biggest still trading is 170,618 GT, just below No. 42.
7 of these 42 ship classes did not exist before 2025. The race to build bigger isn't over.
Gross tonnage measures a ship's enclosed volume, not its weight. Cruise ships score high.
Next: the class of Ever Given, the ship that blocked the Suez Canal for six days in 2021.
MSC Irina carries the most boxes (24,346 TEU), yet 3 container classes outrank it.
No. 1 is 62% bigger than Icon of the Seas, and it's neither a cargo nor a cruise ship.
